bib.title: ComputerRL: Scaling End-to-End Online Reinforcement Learning for Computer Use Agents

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "ComputerRL: Scaling End-to-End Online Reinforcement Learning for Computer Use Agents", Hanyu Lai, Xiao Liu, Yanxiao Zhao et al. (Tsinghua / Z.AI / UCAS; Yuxiao Dong, Jie Tang), arXiv:2508.14040v2, 21 Oct 2025 (preprint; the paper says its algorithm and framework are used in AutoGLM).

COVERAGE: 33 of 33 pages read. Extraction was 75,556 chars and read in full: main text, Tables 1-6, appendices A-G (the references skimmed). Page numbers below are printed page numbers. Figures 2 to 15 are images and were not viewed; only their captions and text were read.

CLAIMS (ranked)

- Reward is a binary, rule-based outcome reward, copied onto every step of a trajectory. A format check also gates it.
  number: 1 or 0 per step
  setup: step-level GRPO. A subset of the human-annotated tasks, each with a rule-based eval function (Sec 3.2).
  quote: "Successfully solved trajectories receive a reward of 1 for every correctly formatted action that contributes to the solution; failed trajectories or improperly formatted actions receive a reward of 0. Unlike conventional approaches that propagate step-wise returns via the Bellman equation, our methodology treats each prompt-response pair as an independent training instance with rewards based on the final trajectory outcome."
  where: p6, Sec 3.2 "Reward Design"

- Advantage is normalised over all steps of all G rollouts of a task, not per trajectory.
  number: Ai,j = (ri,j − mean(R)) / std(R), with R = {r_u,v} over u=1..G, v=1..L_u
  setup: step-level GRPO. The loss is averaged over total steps (1/ΣLi), with PPO clipping and a KL term.
  quote: "All steps from the same task are grouped, and the advantage Ai,j is computed for each step."
  where: p6, Sec 3.2
  The paper does not say how it computes the std when every reward is identical.

- RL gives a large gain over BC, then plateaus. Entropulse restores entropy, and a second RL phase adds more.
  number: BC 31.9, RL1 42.0, Entropulse 41.5, RL2 45.8 (average success %, OSWorld)
  setup: Qwen2.5-14B backbone, OSWorld, 5-domain split (Table 3). Untrained baseline 15.2.
  quote: "Starting from the backbone, Behavior Cloning (BC) establishes a solid foundation with 31.9%. The first RL phase (RL1) yields substantial gains, increasing the performance to 42.0% (+10.1%). Interestingly, Entropulse phase maintains similar performance (41.5%) while significantly increasing action entropy... The RL2 phase achieves the best performance at 45.8% (+3.8% from RL1)"
  where: p8-9, Sec 4.3, Table 3
  Workflow domain: 10.8 to 27.2.

- Entropulse is a recipe of alternating RL and SFT. RL is run until it plateaus. Successful rollouts from all earlier policies are kept and used as an SFT set. RL is then resumed.
  number: plateau at about 180 steps; about 130,000 extra steps of SFT data; SFT learning rate 5e-6 (BC used 1e-5); RL resumed to 360 total steps
  setup: Appendix D. The BC checkpoint used for RL is the 1-epoch one "for diversity". Successful trajectories are chosen at random per unique task.
  quote: "We initially train the BC policy (using the 1-epoch checkpoint for diversity) for 180 steps, after which performance improvements began to plateau. At this point, we collect rollouts during RL, perform task-level random selection, and curate approximately 130,000 additional steps of data for Entropulse training."
  where: p20, App D. Main text p6-7, Sec 3.3.
  The motivation is that RL entropy falls and KL rises. Raising the clip threshold (DAPO-style) "attenuates the decline in entropy but significantly slows down policy improvement".

- Entropulse beats continued RL with only a reference-model reset.
  number: none given in the text. Fig 1b and Fig 5 show reward curves with 95% CIs, with reward axis about 0.30-0.55 and entropy axis about 0.10-0.30.
  setup: both arms reset the reference model, for a fair comparison.
  quote: "The results demonstrate that incorporating Entropulse increases the model's entropy, thereby restoring its exploratory capacity. This enhanced exploration substantially scales the effective training steps, ultimately leading to improved overall performance."
  where: p8-9, Sec 4.3 "RL Scalability", Fig 5
  This is a qualitative claim read off a curve. No final-score table separates Entropulse from the reset-only arm.

- The API-GUI action space, which adds generated APIs to GUI actions, strongly outperforms GUI-only.
  number: 26.2 vs 11.2 average (+134%). Office 27.9 vs 6.2. Professional 41.6 vs 14.3.
  setup: GPT-4o as the agent, OSWorld, no RL (Table 3).
  quote: "the API-GUI strategy achieves an average success rate of 26.2%, representing a 134% improvement over the GUI-only approach (11.2%)."
  where: p8, Sec 4.3
  Related claim: tasks take "at most 1/3 of the steps required by the strongest baseline approaches". No step counts are tabulated (p8).

- Headline result: AutoGLM-OS-9B reaches 48.9% on OSWorld.
  number: 48.9±0.5 (GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking); 48.1±1.0 (GLM-4-9B-0414). OSWorld-Verified 48.0 and 47.3.
  setup: OSWorld, 9B open models.
  Comparators: OpenAI CUA o3 42.9, UI-TARS-1.5 42.5, Agent S2 w/ Gemini-2.5-Pro 41.4, Claude 4.0 Sonnet 30.7. On OSWorld-Verified, Claude 4.0 Sonnet is 43.9 and Agent S2 is 45.8. ARPO (7B) 29.9.
  quote: "achieving a success rate of 48.9% (with 66% performance gain from RL), outperforming other state-of-the-art models including OpenAI CUA o3 (42.9%), UI-TARS-1.5 (42.5%), and Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4 (30.7%)."
  where: p3 and Table 1, p7
  The "66% gain from RL" is stated without a baseline. 30.7 (SFT) to 48.9 is about 59%, and 48.9 over 29.5 would give 66%, so the baseline is unclear. The setup for the Fig 1a SFT bar is unstated.

- OfficeWorld (180 tasks from SpreadsheetBench, PPTC and in-house Writer tasks): the 9B models beat o3.
  number: 43.3 (GLM-4.1V) and 41.1 (GLM-4-9B) vs o3 33.9, GPT-4.1 25.0, Claude 4.0 Sonnet 24.4
  setup: same framework with tools for every model. Excel 58.3 for both RL models.
  quote: "We employ the same framework (with tools) and test settings to ensure a fair comparison."
  where: p8, Table 2
  The authors built this benchmark themselves.

- Error breakdown of failures.
  number: 34.4% multiple-app; 25.8% vision; 25.6% illusion; 14.2% others (the percentages were read off the Fig 6 legend and may not match their labels exactly)
  setup: case study; the sample size is not stated.
  where: p9, Fig 6, Sec 4.4

- Training data and infrastructure.
  number: 8k tasks; 180k+ correct steps for BC; 1,000+ parallel desktops in Fig 3, "several thousands" in text; 103 APIs across 6 apps
  setup: BC data from multiple closed LLMs. Tasks are stratified by pass rate: fully solved, partial and unsolved. Partial tasks get an SFT'd model to sample more. Unsolved tasks get random per-action model choice from a pool. Only successful trajectories are kept.
  quote: "retaining only successful trajectories (180k+ correct steps)"
  where: p5-6, p16 (Table 5: Code 12, Chrome 11, Calc 27, Impress 22, Writer 19, VLC 12)
  Infrastructure: qemu-in-docker VMs, gRPC multi-node cluster, AgentRL fully async with a limited replay buffer to reduce off-policy bias.

- RL hyperparameters (Table 6).
  number: batch 32 tasks; 16 responses per prompt; concurrency 1024; max turns 30; max response 2,048 tokens; max prompt 63,488; temperature 0.8; actor LR 1e-6; clip 0.2; KL low_var_kl coef 0.0003; entropy coef 0.0; γ=1, λ=1
  setup: GRPO advantage estimator, FSDP, bf16.
  where: p21, Table 6

LIMITS
- Reward is outcome-only and binary. It is credited to every format-valid step of a successful trajectory, so wasted or lucky steps get the same reward. No ablation of reward shaping, partial credit or reward hacking is given.
- The reward rests on hand-written eval functions (human-annotated, 10 annotators). Task coverage is the bottleneck. The authors list robustness to unseen apps and pop-ups and long-horizon autonomy as future work (App F).
- The ablation (Table 3) uses Qwen2.5-14B, while headline results use GLM-4 9B models. Single runs; Table 3 has no CIs. The Entropulse gain over RL1 is only +3.8 points.
- Comparisons against proprietary agents mix scaffolds, and some baseline numbers are missing. OfficeWorld is the authors' own benchmark.
- Entropulse is motivated empirically. No theory is given, and the number of SFT rounds or alternations beyond one is untested. The paper reports only one pulse, though it describes the method as alternating.
- Safety is acknowledged as an open problem (App F.3): agents that can modify files and run unbounded actions need permissioning.

BUILDS ON
- GRPO (Shao et al., 2024 DeepSeekMath; Guo et al., 2025 DeepSeek-R1), PPO (Schulman et al., 2017) and DAPO (Yu et al., 2025, the clip-threshold idea).
- AgentRL (Zhang et al., 2025) for async training, AgentBench (Liu et al., 2023), OSWorld (Xie et al., 2024), AReaL (Fu et al., 2025), Verl/HybridFlow (Sheng et al., 2025).
- ARPO (Lu et al., 2025), ZeroGUI (Yang et al., 2025b), UI-TARS (Qin et al., 2025), Agent S2 (Agashe et al., 2025).
- Behaviour cloning (Bain & Sammut 1995). Test-case generation (Li & Yuan 2024). API creation (Yang et al., 2024a; Wang et al., 2024).

CODE
Only the prompt template, with the output format (p18):
"< think > {** YOUR - PLAN - AND - THINKING **} </ think > ```python {** ONE - LINE - OF - CODE **} ```"
Rules in the prompt: one line of code per turn; call `Agent.exit(success=False)` rather than repeat actions; history keeps thinking, action and feedback but omits the environment state. Action space (Table 4): open_app, click, type, drag_and_drop, scroll, switch_window, hotkey, quote, wait, exit.

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p1): (a) OSWorld bar chart; (b) reward curves, Entropulse vs baseline, 95% CI. Shows the headline claim at a glance.
- Fig 4 (p6): three-stage pipeline: BC cold start, RLVR, then Entropulse with RLVR (performance, entropy and KL arrows). This is the best single picture of the recipe.
- Fig 5 (p9): reward and entropy over steps 0-360 for RL Phase 1, RL Phase 2 and Entropulse + RL Phase 2. Shows the entropy dip and recovery.
- Fig 6 (p9): error distribution pie.
- Fig 3 (p4): the async rollout and trainer architecture.
- Figs 7-8: annotation guidelines (eval function types, compare_with_golden, check_list). These show how verifiable rewards were authored.

PROBLEMS
- Extraction is clean apart from run-together words and the garbled Fig 1 text. The Fig 6 percentage-to-label mapping is ambiguous.
- No embedded instructions found in the PDF text.
- Figures were not viewed; Fig 1b and Fig 5 give no extracted numeric values.
- The claim "66% performance gain from RL" has no stated baseline.
